name: OVHcloud GPU instances

modes.label: h200-1920, on-demand (×8 node)
modes.note: Source: https://www.ovhcloud.com/en/public-cloud/prices/ ESTIMATOR EXCLUDED: Bundled node count/CPU/RAM constraints are not enforceable in current engine schema. Exact researched rate remains in gpu.json.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

free.conditions: First Public Cloud project; activate at creation; valid one month; valid payment method required; one voucher per person; standard direct OVHcloud Public Cloud charges only.

caveats: International USD page, ex VAT. Bundled CPU/RAM/storage. Region selection affects rate/availability. IPv4 starts billing separately October 1, 2026; not yet applicable on research date. Page mislabels multiple GPU memory technologies: do not copy HBM2 claims for L4/H100.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

t1-45 (Tesla V100) and rtx5000-28 (Quadro RTX 5000) are older-generation GPUs but still listed and orderable on the live price page (2026-09-28: t1-45 $0.77/h in BHS5/GRA5/GRA7/GRA9; rtx5000-28 $0.60/h in GRA9 only), so they are not flagged legacy. Their GPU names are outside the engine GPU ladder, so they are never used as an H100 substitute.

fleet.verification: Valid payment method; account age and paid invoices affect eligibility.
fleet.notes: Project quotas can be requested in Control Panel subject to eligibility; support handles CPU/RAM/storage and special needs. Numeric fresh-account quotas vary and were not established; GPU approval and stock must be checked separately.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The data on your local disk will be stored in a snapshot automatically created once the instance is shelved. Data stored in the memory and elsewhere will not be retained.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: shelving the instance (called 'Suspend' in the OVHcloud Control Panel, 'shelve' in OpenStack); disk only, memory NOT included; snapshot is restored on unshelve and then deleted; only the snapshot is billed while shelved. No idle/timeout trigger. Warning in same guide: shelving T1/T2-180 GPU (and IOPS) flavors loses data on NVMe passthrough drives. Other stop modes: OpenStack 'suspend' stores VM state incl. memory on disk but keeps full billing; 'pause' keeps state in RAM. Scheduled automatic instance backups also exist (not counted here).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Backups can be used to restore your instance to a previous state or to create a new, identical instance.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Instance backups (Glance image snapshots) via Control Panel, OVHcloud API (POST /cloud/project/{serviceName}/region/{regionName}/instance/{instanceId}/snapshot) or OpenStack; optional distant copy in another region; disk only (no memory); new instances can boot from them (template/clone). Volume snapshots/backups for Block Storage too.

harness_api.note: Plain OpenStack GPU VMs; no first-party agent-harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: You can allow or block certain incoming or outgoing connections using security groups.
egress_allowlist.note: OpenStack Neutron security groups (egress rules by protocol/port/CIDR or remote group), applied per port on public and private networks, enforced outside the guest. Default group allows all in/out; a new group allows only outgoing until you edit rules. No hostname/domain rules.

ingress_rules.quote: all the network ports (public and private) will allow every connection when you start an instance
ingress_rules.note: That is the default-group behaviour; custom security groups with ingress rules (protocol/port/CIDR) can be applied to public and private ports; instances can also be private-network-only (vRack) or use floating IPs.

guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VM with root; iptables/nftables/ufw in the guest work as on any Linux VM.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy for Public Cloud instances; secrets are whatever you put in the VM (cloud-init/user data, env, or fetched from OVHcloud KMS/secret services). Not documented as a feature.

volume_attach.quote: It is possible to create additional disks for your Public Cloud instances.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage (Cinder) volumes attached to instances; resizable, snapshot/backup-able; can also boot from volume.

volume_shared.quote: This service offers managed NFS shares on private networks, supporting ReadWriteMany (RWX) access across multiple instances or Kubernetes pods.
volume_shared.note: File Storage Service (OpenStack Manila, NFSv4) read-write, over private network with access rules (accessLevel rw/ro). Also Enterprise File Storage (NetApp), HA-NAS, and 'Classic Multi-Attach Block Storage' in 3AZ regions (needs a cluster FS such as OCFS2).

isolation.quote: The technology used (pci_passthrough) allows the instance's operating system to control the GPU in exactly the same way a physical machine would.
isolation.note: OVHcloud Public Cloud GPU instances are OpenStack Nova instances (full VMs on KVM) with GPU PCI passthrough, not containers or microVMs.

image_oci.quote: Custom Images: You can import your own images in QCOW2 or RAW format, providing full control over your environment
image_oci.note: Instances boot from OpenStack/Glance VM disk images (QCOW2/RAW) that you import yourself, not from a Docker/OCI container image; not offered: outside the product's scope (it's a VM, not a container runtime).

docker_inside.quote: Pre-configured Applications: Images that come with software such as cPanel, Plesk, Docker, or NVIDIA GPU Cloud (NGC).
docker_inside.note: Full VM with root access; Docker is offered as a ready-made app image and can also be installed manually on any Linux image.

desktop.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. OVHcloud GPU instances are IaaS VMs (SSH/RDP access); no managed VNC/streamed-desktop or browser product is offered.

browser.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed/preinstalled browser product; users could install one themselves on the VM.

computer_use.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Plain IaaS GPU VM; no screenshot/click computer-use API.

anti_bot.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Generic GPU cloud VM; no stealth/fingerprinting product feature.

captcha_solving.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Generic GPU cloud VM; no CAPTCHA-solving product feature.

egress_ip_type.quote: Instances in Public Mode are exposed to the public Internet directly via IPv4/IPv6.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard datacenter-assigned public/floating IPv4 addresses; not residential/mobile.

ssh.quote: Find out how to create key pairs for OpenSSH on your local device and use them to establish secure connections to your instance
ssh.note: SSH key management is a core part of instance creation/access.

fork.quote: Creating a new instance with the backup as a template in order to duplicate the original instance, for example if you are configuring a load balancing infrastructure.
fork.note: New instances can be created (cloned) from an instance backup/snapshot.

fork_running.quote: Backups can be used to restore your instance to a previous state or to create a new, identical instance.
fork_running.note: OpenStack/Glance instance snapshotting (createImage) does not require stopping the instance first, though a brief pause internally may occur; not explicitly documented as requiring shutdown.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The data on your local disk will be stored in a snapshot automatically created once the instance is shelved. Data stored in the memory and elsewhere will not be retained.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Backups/snapshots and clones are disk-only; running processes/memory state are not preserved when cloning.

wake_on_request.quote: The data on your local disk will be stored in a snapshot automatically created once the instance is shelved.
wake_on_request.note: Shelving/pausing/stopping are all manual actions (Control Panel/API/OpenStack); no documented feature that auto-wakes a stopped instance on an inbound network request.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Learn how to shelve, pause or suspend a Public Cloud instance to temporarily free resources while keeping your IP address, and understand the billing impact of each option
auto_stop_idle.note: Shelve/pause/suspend are all customer-initiated actions; no documented idle-detection auto-stop feature for GPU/Compute instances.

live_resize.quote: this manipulation causes the instance to be shut down for the time of the operation.
live_resize.note: Resizing (changing flavor/CPU/RAM) requires shutting down the instance.

agent_harnesses.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Plain OpenStack GPU VMs; no preinstalled/offered coding-agent harness templates.

own_agent_api.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No first-party browser/computer-use/research agent API for this product.

mcp_server.quote: Getting started with the MCP server for domain names
mcp_server.note: OVHcloud ships an MCP server only for Domain Names (per docs index); no MCP server for Public Cloud Compute/GPU instances.

lang_python.quote: Linux Distributions: Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and others. These images are ready to use for web servers, development environments, and general-purpose workloads.
lang_python.note: Plain OS images; no guaranteed/managed Python runtime out of the box (user installs/manages it themselves, though many Linux base images ship python3).

lang_node.quote: Linux Distributions: Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and others. These images are ready to use for web servers, development environments, and general-purpose workloads.
lang_node.note: Plain OS images; Node.js is not preinstalled and must be installed by the user.

public_ipv4.quote: Instances in Public Mode are exposed to the public Internet directly via IPv4/IPv6.
public_ipv4.note: Public IPv4 assigned by default in Public Mode; IPv4 will start being billed separately from Oct 1, 2026 per pricing page caveat.

inbound_https.quote: Instances in Public Mode are exposed to the public Internet directly via IPv4/IPv6.
inbound_https.note: Any port including 443 can be reached directly on the instance's public IP; HTTPS termination/cert setup is the customer's responsibility (or via the optional Load Balancer with Let's Encrypt).

egress_http_rules.quote: You can allow or block certain incoming or outgoing connections using security groups.
egress_http_rules.note: Security groups filter by protocol/port/CIDR (network layer), not HTTP method/path level rules.

static_egress_ip.quote: Assign a Floating IP (Reusable) (persistent and reusable).
static_egress_ip.note: A Floating IP is persistent/reusable and can be kept fixed as the instance's public (and thus effectively outbound-identifiable) address across rebuilds.

macos.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. OVHcloud Public Cloud GPU instances are Linux/Windows OpenStack VMs; no macOS option.

arm64.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
arm64.note: All listed GPU flavors (A10, A100, H100, H200, L4, L40S, RTX5000, V100) run on x86_64 hosts; no ARM GPU instance flavor is offered.

self_host.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is OVHcloud's own managed public cloud offering; not distributed as self-hostable software.

byoc.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. OVHcloud runs the infrastructure in its own datacentres; not deployed into a customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: GPU instances are technically similar to the instances from the older range, but they also have a graphics card
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Built on OpenStack (open source) under the hood, but OVHcloud's managed GPU cloud service itself is not an open-source product.

soc2.quote: SOC 1, 2, 3 — AICPA certification SSAE 16/ISAE 3402 Type 2 for control over financial reporting
soc2.note: Company-wide compliance page lists SOC 1/2/3; not confirmed to be scoped specifically per-product to Public Cloud GPU instances.

hipaa.quote: HIPAA & HITECH — Compliance with the United States Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act in our US datacentres.
hipaa.note: Stated as applicable in OVHcloud's US datacentres; the GPU instance flavors researched here are hosted in EU/Canada regions (GRA/SBG/BHS), so applicability to this specific product/region is not confirmed.

sso.quote: Learn how to associate your Okta service with your OVHcloud account via SAML 2.0
sso.note: SAML 2.0 SSO (AD FS, Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta) is available at the OVHcloud account level, which governs access to Public Cloud projects.

eu_data_residency.note: GPU instances are available in EU regions (e.g. GRA, SBG in France) among the selectable regions.

max_session_h.quote: Learn how to shelve, pause or suspend a Public Cloud instance to temporarily free resources while keeping your IP address, and understand the billing impact of each option
max_session_h.note: These are persistent IaaS VMs billed hourly/monthly that run until the customer stops/deletes them; no maximum session duration is imposed.
